stages.name: Criterion A – Introduction and research
checklist: Pick one narrow, testable aspect of the 2027 brief (membranes, osmosis, food preservation) and write it as a single research question.
Research the biology behind it from at least two reliable secondary sources, and say how reliable or biased each one is.
Write your own testable hypothesis that gives a biological reason for what you expect.

stages.name: Criterion B – Design and experiment
checklist: Design a fair test: name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, plan repeats, and justify each piece of equipment.
List each hazard with its control, and run the experiment only under your teacher's supervision.
Record every reading with units as you take it, anomalies included, and photograph your set-up.

stages.name: Criterion C – Data and conclusions
checklist: Present your data in labelled tables and graphs with units, and calculate means.
State whether your own figures support the hypothesis, and explain the pattern with biology.
Name specific sources of error and a concrete improvement for each.

stages.name: Criterion D – Scientific literacy and hand-in
checklist: Reflect on what your result means for food preservation or society, and how your thinking changed.
Use the seven SEC headings, each on a new page, within 1,500 words and 20 images: Arial 12 body, 14 bold headings, 1.5 spacing, 20 mm margins, SEC cover page first.
Reference every source in the text and in the list, and acknowledge any AI use (tool, date, prompts, how used).
Export to PDF, print it to check every page is visible, sign Form P.2 and hand it in by 26 February 2027.

brief.task: Investigate one or more aspects of the topic Membranes, Osmosis, Food Preservation: research the biology, then design, run and report on your own experiment.
facts: Temperature, concentration gradient and surface area, which affect the rate of osmosis
A PDF report: 1,500 words and 20 images at most, seven SEC headings

stages.name: Criterion A – Introduction and research
checklist: Pick one reaction and one rate factor your school lab can test safely, and write it as a single research question.
Explain the chemistry in your own words with correct terms and equations, and evaluate how reliable each source is.
Write a testable hypothesis backed by collision theory or another chemical reason.

stages.name: Criterion B – Design and experiment
checklist: Design a fair test: name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, plan repeat trials, and justify equipment for the precision you need.
List each hazard with a specific precaution, get your teacher's safety sign-off, and run it only under supervision.
Record observations as well as numbers, with units, and note anomalies and any change to your plan.

stages.name: Criterion C – Data and conclusions
checklist: Present results in labelled tables and graphs with units, and show your working for means and rates.
Explain each trend with chemical theory and state whether the data support your hypothesis.
Identify limitations in your research, design and data, with a specific improvement for each.

stages.name: Criterion D – Scientific literacy and hand-in
checklist: Link your result to a real use in health, sustainability or technology, and show how your research shaped your design.
Use the seven SEC headings, each on a new page, within 1,500 words and 20 images: Arial 12 body, 14 bold headings, 1.5 spacing, 20 mm margins, SEC cover page first.
Reference every source in the text and in the list, and acknowledge any AI use (tool, date, prompts, how used).
Export to PDF, print it to check every page is visible, sign Form P.2 and hand it in by 23 April 2027.

brief.task: Investigate one or more aspects of how the rate of a chemical reaction can be controlled, and link your work to health, sustainability or technology.
facts: Acid–base, decomposition, redox, combination, displacement, precipitation
Concentration, surface area, temperature, pressure, catalyst
A PDF report: 1,500 words and 20 images at most, seven SEC headings

stages.name: Section 1 – Introduction and planning
checklist: Write one SMART research question about one digital work practice and one side only: employers or employees.
Explain why the question matters to business locally, nationally or internationally.
Keep a project plan (objectives, tasks, resources, timeline, risks), share it with your teacher, and log each change and why.

stages.name: Sections 2–3 – Investigation and analysis
checklist: Gather primary and secondary sources that give different perspectives, logging each link and date accessed.
Justify each source or method and judge its reliability and bias.
Analyse patterns, trends and contradictions, tie every point back to the question, and label each image as a Figure (10 images max).
Name the limitations of your question, your data and your analysis.

stages.name: Section 4 – Conclusions
checklist: Answer the question using only what your analysis supports, and say how your planning helped and how your view changed.
Link your findings to a real business or media story and a named cross-cutting theme.

stages.name: Overall coherence – Format and hand-in
checklist: Use the five SEC headings, each on a new page, within 1,500 words: Arial 12 body, 14 bold headings, 1.5 spacing, 20 mm margins, SEC cover page first.
Cite every source in the text and in References, and acknowledge any AI use (tool, date, how used).
Export to PDF, print it to check every page is visible, hand it in by 12 March 2027 and sign Form P.2.

brief.task: Investigate how a work practice that uses digital technology is impacting either employers or employees, supported by primary and/or secondary data.
facts: Digitalisation is raising productivity, disrupting traditional roles and changing the world of work
One digital work practice, and one side only: employers or employees
A PDF report: 1,500 words and 10 images at most, five SEC headings

stages.name: Stage 1 – Introduction
checklist: Pick one of the six 2027 SEC topics and write one testable hypothesis or aim that names the place and what you will measure.

stages.name: Stage 2 – Planning
checklist: List the information you need, the methods you will use, and which sources are primary and which secondary (at least 60% primary).

stages.name: Stage 3 – Gathering information
checklist: Describe two methods in your own words: the equipment and what it measured, how you recorded data, and how many sites, readings or responses.
Acknowledge your secondary sources, and explain problems you met and how they affected the data.

stages.name: Stage 4 – Results, conclusions, evaluation
checklist: State your main results with figures from your own data, referring to each graph.
Say whether the hypothesis is supported and compare your findings with established theory.
Name specific weaknesses in your method, with an improvement for each.

stages.name: Stage 5 – Presentation of results
checklist: Present results in at least two different graph types, each hand-drawn with a title, labels, units and key, and add them as images to the booklet's image pages (no graphing software).
Reference every source, including any AI use, sign the authentication declaration and submit the digital booklet to your teacher by 16 April 2027.

brief.task: Complete a report on one of the six SEC topics below, in the digital Geographical Investigation Reporting Booklet.
list: A study of the evolution of settlement over time in a local urban or rural setting.
The economic and/or environmental impact of one economic activity in a local area.
The role of geomorphic processes in forming one landform in a fluvial, coastal or glacial environment.
Water pollution: a study of a local water source.
The impact of geology on shaping the landscape in a local area.
The relationship between traffic management and residential land use in a local area.
facts: The digital Reporting Booklet: 1,000 typed words at most, hand-drawn illustrations added as images
The same six topics at Higher and Ordinary level

source.label: SEC Prescribed List of Investigation Topics, 2027

stages.name: Outline plan
checklist: Choose a narrow subject with a dated title, all on or before 1993 (Ireland) or 1992 (Europe and the wider world), and get your teacher's approval.
Justify why it is historically significant, state 3–5 aims about the subject, and explain your research approach step by step.
Cite three sources (two at Ordinary level), primary or specialist secondary and not textbooks, with author, title and publisher or date.

stages.name: Evaluation of sources
checklist: For every source you cited, say whether it is primary or secondary and give its relevance, a strength and a weakness, then compare them.

stages.name: Extended essay
checklist: Write an introduction, a logical body and a conclusion that answers each of your aims, within the word range for your level.
Use accurate evidence from all your sources, footnote quotations, and treat the issues fairly from more than one viewpoint.

stages.name: Review of the research process
checklist: Review your own research honestly: whether each aim was achieved, the real problems you met and what you would change.
Proofread, convert to PDF, print it to check every page is visible, and sign the authentication form before the SEC deadline.

brief.task: There is no set topic. With your teacher, choose a narrow, historically significant subject and research it in depth from your own sources.
facts: Nothing after 1993 for Irish history, or after 1992 for European and wider history
At least three (two at Ordinary level): primary or specialist secondary, not school textbooks
The digital RSR booklet: outline plan, evaluation of sources, extended essay with a review
2027 date TBC by the SEC (mid-April in past years)

pe.title: Physical Activity Project (PAP)
pe.summary: The PAP is 20% of Physical Education. Pick a competitive sport and a role, analyse your performance, set three goals with a training plan each, retest, and submit one 1,600-word PDF with three short videos.

brief.task: There is no topic brief. Choose a competitive sport with a Sport Ireland-affiliated governing body and a role (performer or coach/choreographer), in a different activity area from your Performance Assessment.
facts: A competitive sport with a Sport Ireland-affiliated governing body, as performer or coach/choreographer, over 8 to 10 weeks
One PDF booklet of 1,600 words at most (Arial 12, 28 pages) and three MP4 videos totalling 4 minutes at most, one per section
Section A 25, Section B 45 (three goals), Section C 20, overall coherence 10
PAP mid-December 2026 (2026 cycle: 12 December); exact date to be set by the SEC

source.label: NCCA guidelines for the Physical Activity Project

stages.name: Choose and analyse (Section A)
checklist: Pick a competitive sport with a Sport Ireland-affiliated governing body and a role, in a different activity area from your Performance Assessment, and get your teacher to confirm both.
Test every area that matters in your sport, present the data in detail and compare it with referenced normative data.
Interpret what each result means for your performance, linking to your sport and to theory.

stages.name: Goals and training (Section B)
checklist: Set three distinct SMART goals from different areas, each drawn from your Section A data.
Write one individualised training plan per goal in a table, applying a wide range of principles of training.
Give each goal a rationale linked to theory and a reflection based on really doing the training, and film that training.

stages.name: Retest and conclude (Section C)
checklist: Retest everything from Section A under the same conditions and state for each goal whether you achieved it, with numbers and a reason.
Reflect on the effect of the training, including unintended outcomes, and give realistic next steps.

stages.name: Format and submit
checklist: Link Sections A, B and C, and make the three videos support the text in each section.
Stay inside every limit: 1,600 words, 16 images (4, 8 and 4), 4 minutes of video, no collages or text in video.
Reference every source, proofread the printed PDF and sign Form P.2.

pe-performance.subject: pe
pe-performance.title: Performance Assessment
pe-performance.summary: The Performance Assessment is 30% of Physical Education, marked out of 150. You submit one video of up to 8 minutes of your best performance in one of your three studied activities, in a different area from your PAP.

brief.task: There is no topic brief. Choose one of your three studied activities, in a different physical activity area from your Physical Activity Project, and record your best performance in class between January and March.
facts: One of your three studied activities, in a different area from the PAP
One MP4 of 8 minutes at most, a single best performance, with two mandatory text slides and up to four optional ones
Skill and technique 80, tactics 20, rules 10, safe practice 10, overall performance 30 (150 in total)
Late March 2027 (2026 cycle: 23 March); exact date to be set by the SEC

source.label: NCCA guidelines for the Performance Assessment

stages.name: Choose your activity
checklist: Pick an activity from a different area to your PAP and agree it with your teacher.
Plan to show it in more than one context, such as a conditioned practice and a full game, and check the specification's list of skills.

stages.name: Prepare and practise
checklist: Practise every listed skill so you can show a wide variety, on both sides where the activity allows.
Rehearse under pressure and learn the rules, tactics and safety procedures of your activity.

stages.name: Skill and technique
checklist: Show accurate, consistent skills that hold up over repetitions.
Perform with control and fluency, and keep your technique stable under pressure.

stages.name: Tactics, rules and safety
checklist: Use tactics, strategies or composition that clearly help the performance, and show every required element.
Follow every rule and code and show a warm-up, a cool-down and safe use of equipment and attire.

stages.name: Overall performance, film and submit
checklist: Show confident, consistent performance in a range of contexts, in complete form within 8 minutes.
Meet every video rule: be identifiable throughout, no speed changes, collages, music or extra text, and a correct introductory slide.
Name the MP4 to the SEC convention and check the late-March 2027 date.

home-economics.title: Food Studies Practical Coursework

stages.name: Section 1 – Investigation
checklist: Do the number of assignments your teacher confirms (2027 arrangements: two of the five, best two counted), with a different fresh-food dish for each.
Answer every command word in the brief, cover the area's recording criteria, suggest a range of dishes before choosing, and cite every source, AI included.

stages.name: Section 2 – Planning and preparation
checklist: Give the dish name, recipe source, exact quantity and cost of every ingredient, the total cost, and all key equipment.

stages.name: Section 3 – Implementation
checklist: Do the practical in class under supervision, then write up the procedure step by step, the key factors you considered, and the safety and hygiene points.

stages.name: Section 4 – Evaluation
checklist: Write evaluation (a) on the implementation and (b) on the specific requirement under separate headings, each backed by evidence from your practical and what you would change.
Keep the booklet in Arial 12 with 1.5 spacing, check no box has overflowed, convert to PDF, print-check it and sign Form P.2.

brief.task: Food Studies: complete the 2027 assignments in the SEC coursework journal, each with an investigation, planning, a supervised practical and an evaluation.
list: Area A: the diet of older people, with menus and one main course cooked.
Area A: iron deficiency, with menus to reduce the risk and one main course cooked.
Area B: commercial filo or puff pastry, with one sweet or savoury dish cooked.
Area D: marinades, their types and principles, with one marinated dish cooked.
Area E: a descriptive rating test of two granola brands on six attributes, with star diagrams.
facts: Two of the five under the 2027 arrangements; confirm with your teacher

home-economics.summary: Food Studies is the practical coursework journal, worth 20% of Home Economics: each assignment is recorded as an investigation, planning, a supervised practical and an evaluation. It was due on 2 November 2026.

home-economics-textiles.subject: home-economics
home-economics-textiles.title: Textiles, Fashion and Design Coursework
home-economics-textiles.summary: Textiles, Fashion and Design coursework is only for Elective 2 students and is worth 10% of Home Economics (marked out of 100: design folder 25, garment 75). You design a holiday outfit for a young person, make one garment from it with two of three prescribed processes, and hand both in by 6 April 2027.

brief.task: Design and sketch an outfit for a young person to wear on holiday, set out the design specifications, then make and evaluate one garment from it, supported by a design folder.
list: Theme: our values, interests and personality can be expressed through our holiday wardrobe.
The outfit can be knitted, crocheted or machine stitched.
The garment must include two of: button/s and buttonhole/s, darts or shaping, a pocket.
Individual work only, done in class under your teacher's supervision, with your examination number on the folder and the garment.
facts: Only Elective 2 students do it, and they may only answer Question 2 in Section C of the written paper
10% of your Home Economics grade (70% written exam, 20% Food Studies)

source.label: SEC 2027 Textiles, Fashion and Design Elective Practical Coursework Assignment Brief

stages.name: Brief, theme research and design folder
checklist: List the brief's key requirements and constraints: young person, holiday, theme, two processes, 6 April 2027.
Explore the theme in sketches of the full outfit, then name the garment you will make.
Justify the outfit and garment with reasons, and outline your plan of work in order.

stages.name: Make the garment
checklist: Include two of the three processes (buttons and buttonholes, darts or shaping, pocket) and execute each neatly.
Show a range of textile skills beyond Junior Cycle level, all done in class under supervision.
Make the theme clearly identifiable in the garment.

stages.name: Design quality and finish
checklist: Apply design principles (balance, emphasis, proportion, rhythm) and show where in the garment.
Trim, check and press the garment so it is ready to present.

stages.name: Record, evaluate and submit
checklist: Record the work sequence, with a note on how you did each mandatory process.
Evaluate the garment against the brief: difficulties, how you fixed them, and modifications.
Put your examination number on the folder and garment, reference every source, and hand in by 6 April 2027.

irish.subject: irish
irish.title: Scrúdú Cainte (oral exam)
irish.summary: The Scrúdú Cainte is 40% of Leaving Cert Irish, 240 marks, with one common test for Higher and Ordinary Level. An SEC examiner records about 15 minutes in your school at Easter: Fáiltiú 5, a poem 35, a Sraith Pictiúr 80 and a Comhrá 120. For 2027 you prepare 10 of the 20 Sraith Pictiúr.

brief.task: There is no topic brief. You prepare the five prescribed poems for 2027, 10 of the 20 Sraith Pictiúr 2027, and conversation topics. On the day you answer the examiner in Irish in four parts.
facts: Oral held in the Easter holidays 2027, dates not yet published (2026: Saturday 28 March to Thursday 2 April)
About 15 minutes, recorded by an SEC examiner in your school
Fáiltiú 5, Léamh na Filíochta 35, Sraith Pictiúr 80, Comhrá 120 (240 in total)
The 5 prescribed poems and 10 of the 20 Sraith Pictiúr 2027 (hand the examiner your list of 10)
One common test for Higher and Ordinary Level

source.label: Department of Education and Youth: Assessment Arrangements 2027 (Irish page)

stages.name: Know the test
stages.marksNote: Not marked, but it sets your plan
checklist: Split your preparation by marks: the conversation is half the test and the picture series a third.
Check you are learning the 2027 and 2028 poems, not the old list.

stages.name: Fáiltiú and poem
checklist: Give name, age, date of birth, address and exam number in full Irish sentences.
Learn each prescribed poem in full and say its title and the poet before you read.

stages.name: Sraith Pictiúr
checklist: Prepare 10 of the 20 Sraith Pictiúr 2027 and write the list of 10 titles for the examiner.
Describe each picture in 5 or 6 sentences in one tense, with a wide range of verbs.
Plan one question to ask about the story and a sentence of your own experience.

stages.name: Comhrá
checklist: Prepare 12 or more topics with a fact, an opinion, the past and a conditional for each.
Give full answers, steer the conversation to what you prepared, and match the tense of each question.

stages.name: Practise and the day
checklist: Speak out loud and record yourself, and do three timed 15-minute mocks before Easter.
Leave your phone outside, bring your list of 10 titles, and use recovery phrases instead of silence.

french.subject: french
french.title: Oral Examination
french.summary: The French oral is 25% of your Higher Level grade. It is a general conversation of about 12 to 15 minutes with an SEC examiner, with an optional document or project you can bring. Four things earn the marks: Communication 30, Structures 30, Vocabulary 20 and Pronunciation 20.

brief.task: Prepare spoken answers on the usual topics (family, school, free time, job, holidays, future plans), optionally one document or project, and practise aloud so the conversation flows when the examiner jumps around.
facts: About 12 to 15 minutes, with an SEC-appointed examiner in your school
Communication 30, Structures 30, Vocabulary 20, Pronunciation 20 (100 in total; split from the Irish Times 2026, not the SEC page)
A document, photo or project of your choice to start a part of the conversation
Same format, worth 80 marks and 20% of the grade
Oral held in the first week of the Easter holidays (2026: 28 March to 2 April); 2027 window not yet published

stages.name: Know the test
checklist: Check your oral date with your school and the SEC window for the Easter holidays.
Learn the four marking headings and what each rewards.

stages.name: Prepare topics and a document
checklist: Write 5 or 6 spoken sentences on each main topic, answering Qui, Où, Quand, Pourquoi.
Choose one document or project and write ten sentences about it in three tenses.

stages.name: Communication
checklist: Answer the question word first, then add a reason and a detail.
Do full mock orals with follow-up questions.
Learn rescue lines for when you freeze or lack a word.

stages.name: Structures
checklist: Put a past, a future and a conditional into each topic answer.
Use five structures you are sure of, such as subjonctif, si + conditionnel, y and en.

stages.name: Vocabulary and pronunciation
checklist: Swap bland words for ten stronger opinion phrases and link words.
Record yourself and fix nasal vowels, liaison and stress.

stages.name: On the day
checklist: Warm up by saying five answers aloud before you go in.
If you freeze, ask for the question again in French and carry on.

spanish.subject: spanish
spanish.title: Oral Examination
spanish.summary: The Spanish oral is a 15-minute conversation with an examiner in March. At Higher Level it is 25 percent of your grade. It has a general conversation (70 marks) and a role-play (30 marks).

brief.task: A 15-minute oral with an SEC examiner: about 10 minutes of general conversation, then one role-play from the SEC cards after one minute to read it.
facts: Oral held in the 2027 window, provisionally Sat 20 to Thu 25 March 2027 (2026 was 28 March to 2 April); your school sets your slot
About 15 minutes: about 10 for conversation, about 5 for the role-play
Higher Level 100 (25 percent): conversation 70, role-play 30. Ordinary Level 80 (20 percent)
Five SEC cards, examiner speaks first, one minute to read, four prepared turns and one unseen question, 6 marks each
No picture series, poem or prepared document

stages.name: Know the format and plan
checklist: Learn the two parts and their marks: conversation 70, role-play 30.
Put your weekly practice slots in a calendar up to 20 March 2027.

stages.name: Build your conversation bank
checklist: Write short answers on each topic in past, present and future.
Learn ideas, not word-for-word blocks, and end answers with a hook.
Learn question words and how to ask for a repeat.

stages.name: Learn the role-plays
checklist: Confirm with your teacher which cards you must prepare and learn all five if unsure.
Write your four turns in your own words and prepare the unseen question.

stages.name: Practise under exam conditions
checklist: Do two full 15-minute mock orals with a card and one minute to read.
Fix speed, pronunciation and tenses from the feedback.

stages.name: General conversation
checklist: Greet in Spanish, answer in full sentences with a reason, and use several tenses.
Correct slips calmly and ask for a repeat if needed.

stages.name: Role-play
checklist: Use the minute to check the tense for each prompt.
Give each prompt fully and answer the final question with a verb and a little extra.

construction-studies.subject: construction-studies
construction-studies.title: Coursework: Design and Realisation
construction-studies.summary: The project is 150 marks: an artefact you make in school plus a design folio. It is 25% of your grade at Higher Level (30% at Ordinary). There is no set theme, so you pick a project you can finish in school and agree it with your teacher.

brief.task: Choose and agree a project with your teacher, make the artefact in school under supervision, and write a design folio (report). No brief is set by the SEC; you choose.
facts: An artefact and a design folio or report
Planning 40, Report 35, Manipulative Skills 40, Completion 35 (150 in total)
The artefact is made entirely in school and never leaves it
Laboratory work is not required in 2027
All coursework complete by Friday 30 April 2027

source.label: SEC Construction Studies 2027 coursework instructions and marking criteria

stages.name: Plan the project
checklist: Agree a project you can finish in school and write down a simple weekly plan to 30 April 2027.
Do relevant research, in your own words, and reference every source including any AI material.
Develop your design through annotated sketches and one working drawing with sizes and joints.

stages.name: Make the artefact
checklist: Mark out accurately and show a range of different joints and processes.
Make everything in school, never take the artefact home, and photograph each stage as you go.

stages.name: Finish and complete
checklist: Finish the artefact well, with sanding, edge shaping and a final finish.
Check the artefact, drawings and folio match, so the work is coherent.

stages.name: Write the design folio
checklist: Record the manufacturing sequence with photos or sketches, step by step.
Write a specific critical appraisal and conclusions from your experience, and present the folio neatly.

stages.name: Sign off and hand in
stages.marksNote: No marks of its own; a breach can mean 0 for the component
checklist: Put your examination number on the artefact and the folio.
Finish by Friday 30 April 2027 and make sure the teacher and principal can validate your work.

construction-studies-practical.subject: construction-studies
construction-studies-practical.title: Practical Test
construction-studies-practical.summary: The Practical Test is a 4 hour hand-tool woodwork test, marked out of 150. It is 25% of your grade at Higher Level (30% at Ordinary). You make a small piece from a drawing and you are marked on marking out, each joint and the finished assembly.

brief.task: In 4 hours in school, make the set piece from the drawing using hand tools only. A battery screwdriver is allowed but machines are not.
facts: 4 hours, Common Level, one paper for Higher and Ordinary
Machine use on a procedure means half marks for it
Late April 2027, not yet published (2026 was 28 to 30 April)

source.label: SEC 2025 Construction Studies marking scheme, Practical Test

stages.name: Prepare and practise
checklist: Practise every joint seen in 2024 and 2025 and time yourself on each.
Learn that sawing and paring are marked cut by cut, so work to the line.

stages.name: Marking out
checklist: Read the whole drawing and make a cutting list before you cut.
Mark out every joint carefully with gauge, square and knife and check sizes.

stages.name: Processing the joints
checklist: Do the highest-mark joints first and cut on the waste side of the line.
Pare every trench to depth and drill holes accurately.

stages.name: Assembly and finish
checklist: Dry fit before gluing and keep the last 20 to 30 minutes for assembly and edge shaping.

stages.name: On the day
checklist: Use hand tools only, write your examination number on the paper and hand the paper and artefact to the Superintendent.

art.subject: art
art.title: Practical Coursework
art.summary: Practical Coursework is 50% of Art, marked out of 250. You choose one theme from the SEC brief, research from primary sources in your Visual Journal, and make Artefact A in class over about 12 weeks. The journal development for Artefact B also counts here, and the realised Artefact B is the practical exam.

brief.task: Choose one theme from the SEC brief. In the SEC Visual Journal, research from primary sources, draw, and develop ideas for two artefacts in two distinctly different areas of practice. Realise Artefact A in class over about 12 school weeks.
facts: 250 marks, 50% of Art. Artefact A is 175 marks and the journal work for Artefact B is 75
SEC Visual Journal (development for A and B) and Artefact A; 2D A5 to A2, 3D up to 1 metre, film 1 to 3 minutes
Investigation 5, primary sources 30, development 40, realised artefact 90, two areas of practice 10, per artefact
2027 dates not yet published. Brief usually January, 12 school weeks; 2026 brief issued 28 Nov 2025, finished Friday 17 April 2026
All work done in school and never taken home; every source referenced, AI included

stages.name: Brief and theme
checklist: Pick the theme that gives you real objects and places you can draw first-hand.
Plan two artefacts in two distinctly different areas of practice, with B small enough for 5 hours.

stages.name: Exploration page
checklist: Show several different ways into your theme, with drawings and your own reasons.
Work directly in the journal with no extra pages or inserts.

stages.name: Primary sources and drawing
checklist: Draw from real objects and places, and from imagination, memory or feeling, in a range of media.
Analyse each source with tone, line, colour and close-up studies.

stages.name: Development and Visual Studies
checklist: Show progression: tested ideas, noted failures and annotated decisions on Development Sheets 1 and 2.
Name the artists whose work changed yours and say what you took from them.

stages.name: Realise Artefact A
stages.marksNote: 90 for the artefact, 10 for two areas of practice
checklist: Make an artefact that clearly follows your journal and uses elements, principles and your chosen media with control.
Finish it dry, labelled and ready to store before the finishing date.

stages.name: Statements and hand-in
checklist: Write the Final Proposals and Artist's Statements, and reference every source.
Leave the journal and artefacts in school and follow the sealing and labelling rules.

art-practical.subject: art
art-practical.title: Invigilated Practical Examination
art-practical.summary: The Invigilated Practical Examination is 20% of Art, marked out of 100. You make Artefact B from scratch in 5 hours, in two 2.5 hour periods, using your Visual Journal. It is marked on the same criteria and common brief as the coursework.

brief.task: Make Artefact B from scratch in a 5-hour invigilated exam, in two periods of 2.5 hours, based on the development work in your Visual Journal. It must be finished, dry and ready for storage at the end.
facts: 100 marks, 20% of Art, on the realised Artefact B
5 hours on one day: two 2.5 hour periods with a break
Personal artefact 30, elements and principles 20, media and techniques 30, impact 10, different area of practice 10
2027 window not yet published. 2026 was Tuesday 21 to Thursday 23 April after coursework ended
Blank start, no prepared materials, no internet; Visual Journal allowed; still-life objects only

stages.name: Plan and prepare
checklist: Choose a medium and size you can finish in 5 hours, different from Artefact A, and test the techniques in your journal.
Agree materials with your teacher, and pack only a journal and permitted objects.

stages.name: First 2.5 hours
checklist: Block in the whole piece before the break, following your journal plan.
Set your focal point, contrast, balance and colour choices early.

stages.name: Second 2.5 hours
stages.marksNote: Criteria H, I and J, 50 marks
checklist: Refine with control of the media you tested, then step back and judge the overall impact.
Finish dry, labelled and ready to store in the last 15 minutes.

stages.name: Know the marking
checklist: Check your plan against F to J: intention, elements, technique, impact, a different area of practice.
Make sure the artefact visibly follows your Artefact B development sheets.

physics.subject: physics
physics.title: Physics in Practice Investigation
physics.summary: A supervised piece of coursework worth 200 marks, 40% of Leaving Cert Physics. For 2027 you investigate domestic sustainability: energy sources, energy use or energy losses in the home. You write a PDF report of at most 1500 words and 20 images, due to your teacher on Friday 11 December 2026.

brief.task: Investigate one or more aspects of domestic sustainability, energy sources, energy usage and/or energy losses, and report on it.
facts: Reducing domestic energy losses while keeping a comfortable indoor environment
SEAI diagram of home energy sources and uses (heating, hot water, cooking, lighting, appliances)
A PDF report: 1,500 words and 20 images at most, seven SEC headings

stages.name: Criterion A – Introduction and research
checklist: Pick one aspect of home energy (a source, a use or a loss) that you can test in one lab session, and write it as a single research question.
Explain the physics in your own words and say how reliable each main source is.
Write a testable hypothesis with a physics reason.

stages.name: Criterion B – Design and experiment
checklist: Design a fair test: name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, plan repeat readings and justify your equipment.
List each hazard with a precaution, get your teacher's sign-off, and book your supervised lab slot now.
Record every reading with units, and note anomalies and any change to your plan.

stages.name: Criterion C – Data and conclusions
checklist: Show results in labelled tables and graphs with units, with working for every calculated quantity.
Explain each trend with physics and say whether the data support your hypothesis.
Name limits in your research, design and data, each with a specific improvement.

stages.name: Criterion D – Scientific literacy and hand-in
checklist: Link your result to a real home-energy issue, and keep the report coherent from the introduction to the conclusion.
Use the seven SEC headings on new pages within 1,500 words and 20 images: Arial 12 at 1.5 spacing, 20 mm margins, SEC cover page first.
Reference every source and any AI use, export to PDF, print to check every page, sign Form P.2 and hand in by 11 December 2026.
